Tickets are sold online, and the expensive ones are often sold out in minutes. Another big difference is that now, half the audience is recording the show on their phones instead of just enjoying it. But our class leader told us not to give up. We worked together really fast, and somehow, we fixed it just in time. We didn't win first prize, but we got a special award for team spirit. I still keep the group photo we took in front of that gate, and we still talk about it when we meet.

sample_answer_ih: Schools today are very different from when I was a student. In my time, teachers mainly used chalk and a blackboard, and we copied everything into our notebooks. Now, my daughter's kindergarten already has smart TVs and projectors, and older students use tablets and laptops for their homework. Another big change is communication. In the past, if I got bad grades, my parents only found out at the parent meeting at the end of the semester. These days, teachers and parents chat in group messages every day, so parents know everything immediately. Also, students now learn more practical skills, like English conversation and computer skills, from a young age. On the other hand, I think students today have even more pressure, because they have extra classes almost every evening. So schools are more modern, but I'm not sure they're more relaxing.
